front-splitters.note: Needs the car raised and a few holes drilled in the bumper underside.

spoilers-wings.note: Drilling the hatch and tapping the brake light feed is best left to a fitter.

body-kits.note: Panel alignment and paint matching decide the result. Book a body shop.

rear-diffusers.note: Some cars need the lower bumper valance trimmed.

grilles.note: The front bumper usually has to come off.

emblems-decals.note: Clean, dry panel and a steady hand. Large graphics are easier with two people.

steering-wheels.note: Wheel swaps involve the airbag: battery off, trained fitter only. Covers are a 20 minute job at home.

gear-knobs.note: Check the thread size before ordering. Pedal covers must be clamped tight.

floor-mats.note: Drop in. Make sure the driver mat locks on the factory hooks.

seat-covers.note: A fitter gets a wrinkle-free result and keeps airbag seams clear.

ambient-lighting.note: Door cards and dash trims come off. Footwell USB kits are a simple home job.

gauges-displays.note: OBD head-up displays plug in at home. Clusters need coding and a specialist.

headlights.note: Bumper removal on most cars, then beam aiming.

tail-lights.note: Usually four nuts and one plug per side. Connected light bars need a fitter.

led-bulbs.note: Same socket as the halogen bulb. Re-aim the beam afterwards.

fog-projectors.note: Retrofit projectors mean opening the headlight. Factory-pocket kits are simpler.

drls.note: Needs an ignition-switched feed and tidy routing.

aux-lights.note: Always wire through the relay harness, never off the headlight feed.

accent-underbody.note: Underbody strips need the car on a lift and sealed connectors.

air-intakes.note: Drop-in filters take minutes. Intake kits need basic hand tools.

exhaust.note: Tips clamp on in 15 minutes. Full systems need a lift and a fitter.

suspension.note: Workshop job with spring compressors, then a four-wheel alignment.

brakes.note: Safety-critical. Fit, bleed and torque at a workshop.

tuning-hardware.note: Throttle controllers plug in at home. Intercoolers and hoses are workshop jobs.

racing-seats.note: Seat mounts are structural. Workshop fit only.

alloy-wheels.note: Tyre shop job: mount, balance and torque to spec.

wheel-hardware.note: Use a torque wrench and re-check after 50 km.

wheel-styling.note: Caliper covers need the wheels off.

tpms.note: External sensors screw on. Internal sensors need a tyre shop.

head-units.note: Dash trim removal and harness coupling. A fitter keeps steering controls and cameras working.

speakers.note: Door cards come off. Check mounting depth against the window track.

subwoofers-amps.note: Fused power cable from the battery and proper earthing are a must.

sound-damping.note: Slow, careful strip-down of the interior. A full car is a day in the workshop.

dash-cams.note: Socket-powered install is a home job. Hardwiring for parking mode suits a fitter.

parking-safety.note: Bumper drilling for sensors and camera calibration for 360 kits.

horns.note: Behind the grille or bumper. Use a relay for twin horns.

roof-racks.note: Two people. Seal any roof fixings properly.

underbody-armour.note: Heavy parts. Bumper swaps can involve sensors and fog lamp wiring.

snorkels.note: A hole is cut in the wing. No going back, so use a specialist.

light-bars.note: Relay harness, sealed roof entry and a tidy switch position.

recovery-gear.note: Ropes and boards need no fitting. A winch needs a rated mount and heavy cabling, so use a fitter.

overland-camping.note: Tents and awnings bolt to an existing rack. Lifting a tent takes two to three people.

side-steps-flares.note: Under-car bolting. Much easier on a lift.

fluids-additives.note: Additives pour into the tank. Brake fluid changes belong in a workshop.

compliance.plate-frames: High Security Registration Plates are mandatory. Frames must not cover any character, the hologram or the laser code. Custom show plates are for display and private land only, and the plate designer tool should say so on screen.
compliance.steering-wheels: A replacement wheel must keep the factory airbag working. Sell wheels with a fitting-partner option and never as an airbag delete.
compliance.seat-covers: Covers for seats with side airbags must use tear-away seams. State this on the product page.
compliance.gauges-displays: Replacement clusters must carry over the true odometer reading. Say so plainly on the page.
compliance.sunshades-organisers: Do not sell tint film. Position removable shades as parking and rear-passenger comfort items and let buyers check local rules for use while driving.
compliance.headlights: Front lamps must show white or yellow light only, with a correct dipped beam. No flashing, red or blue front lighting.
compliance.tail-lights: Rear lamps must stay red, with amber indicators and white reverse light. Heavily smoked lenses can fail inspection.
compliance.led-bulbs: LED bulbs in reflector housings can dazzle oncoming drivers. Recommend projector housings and beam aiming.
compliance.aux-lights: Auxiliary lamps should be switched off and covered in city traffic. Several states fine uncovered high-output lamps.
compliance.accent-underbody: Underbody and coloured exterior lighting is for shows and private land. Red and blue flashing lights are reserved for emergency vehicles. Do not stock strobes.
compliance.exhaust: Tips are cosmetic. Full systems must keep the catalytic converter and stay inside the legal noise limit, so publish a dB(A) figure and label louder systems as track use.
compliance.suspension: Ride-height changes can affect insurance and warranty. Tell buyers to inform their insurer.
compliance.tuning-hardware: Do not sell emissions-delete parts or engine remap files.
compliance.racing-seats: Removing a factory seat can disable its side airbag and belt warning. List as track and motorsport use.
compliance.alloy-wheels: Keep overall rolling diameter within about 3 percent of stock and the wheel inside the wheel arch. Oversized wheels can draw fines and insurance disputes.
compliance.head-units: Describe phone mirroring as compatible with the phone platforms. Do not present the unit as an official product of either platform.
compliance.horns: Stock only single or twin-tone horns within the legal sound limit. No air pressure horns, musical horns or sirens.
compliance.roof-racks: Loads must stay inside the car maker roof limit. State dynamic and static ratings separately.
compliance.underbody-armour: Do not sell add-on bull bars or crash guards: the transport ministry treats them as illegal on public roads. Label replacement off-road bumpers for off-road and private land use and warn about airbag sensors.
compliance.light-bars: Light bars are for off-road use and should be covered on public roads. Ship a cover with every bar.
compliance.jerry-cans-storage: Cans ship empty. Add a note that fuel carried outside the tank must be in an approved container and within legal limits.
compliance.fluids-additives: Liquids are restricted on air freight. Ship by surface and show a longer delivery estimate.
compliance.emergency-gear: Lithium jump starters and pressurised extinguishers are restricted on air freight. Ship by surface.
compliance.hoodies-jackets: Keep each garment at or under Rs 2,500 sale value to stay in the 5 percent GST slab. Above that the rate is 18 percent.

design.titleFormula: Addon <Line> <what it is>, <key spec or finish> (<pack size>) for <Make Model> (<year range>)
namingRules: No replica naming such as "X-style", and no carmaker trim names used as styles.
No trademarked material names. Use suede-touch and soft-touch leatherette.
Titles say wireless phone mirroring. The spec table may say it works with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, as a compatibility statement.
Car make and model names appear only in the fitment clause.
treeDecisions: Car brand is a fitment filter, not a category.
The reference menu of universal mods by body type became the bodyType fitment.
Wheels have their own category because they are the biggest enthusiast purchase and need a bolt-pattern filter.
Car care and emergency gear have a category because they are the volume lines.
There is no bull bar, strobe light or pressure horn subcategory.

shipClasses.freight: Heavier or oversized, needs a surface courier quote

design.seedRule: In each subcategory the first N titlePatterns are the seed products, where N is seedPlan[subcategory]. seedProducts lists them flattened with SKUs.

recommendations: Seed from seedProducts. Generate each description from the subcategory blurb, the spec template examples and the install note rather than hand-writing 140 descriptions.

Give fitment its own tables: makes, models, generations, and a product-fitment table with the five fitment types. Shop by Car Brand, the garage and the fitment badge on product cards all read from it.
Drive the product page spec table from specTemplates. Store specs as key and value pairs per product so the admin panel can edit them without a schema change.
Sell wheels by bolt pattern. Filter by diameter and bolt pattern first, show the confident models from vehicles.pcdReference as fits, and ask buyers of any other car to confirm their pattern.
Show install effort on every product page: a five-step difficulty meter, the time label and a fitter-advised badge. For fitter-advised products, offer a fitting-partner enquiry at checkout.
Show the compliance notice where a subcategory has one, and add an off-road and show use badge for underbody glow, light bars, off-road bumpers and loud exhaust systems.
Keep hoodies and jackets at Rs 2,499 or less so they stay in the 5 percent GST slab, and compute apparel GST from the sale price.

Use ship class in checkout: free or flat shipping for small and medium, a surcharge for bulky, a quoted or longer delivery for freight. Block cash on delivery for freight items and above an order value the owner sets.
Display prices the Indian way: lakh grouping (Rs 1,19,999), MRP struck through, percent off, and inclusive of all taxes under the price.
Illustrate the 33 base art kinds first and use artKinds.extended as the fallback for the other 28.
List popular models first in the vehicle selector, and keep the discontinued Polo, Vento, Rapid, EcoSport, Endeavour and Figo because their owners are active buyers.
Before a real launch, have an accountant confirm the HSN rows marked verify, and check bolt patterns for every model before claiming wheel fitment by model.

pricingHabits: MRP is shown struck through with a percent-off figure. Marketplace listings run 25 to 65 percent under MRP.
Body kits and spoilers are sold unpainted by default, with painting as a paid option.
Wheels are priced per wheel on maker sites and per set of four in buying guides. Addon sells sets of four.

points: GST collapsed into two main slabs, 5 and 18 percent, from 22 September 2025.
Parts and accessories of motor vehicles (HSN 8708) are a uniform 18 percent. They were split between 18 and 28 before.
Vehicle lighting and signalling equipment (HSN 8512) is listed at 18 percent.
Garments are 5 percent up to Rs 2,500 sale value per piece and 18 percent above. The test is per piece and on sale value, not MRP.
Carpets and textile floor coverings (HSN 5701 to 5705) moved from 12 to 5 percent. This only matters if a mat is a true textile carpet.

Bull bars and crash guards: in December 2017 the road transport ministry told states that fitting them breaks Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act, with penalties under Sections 190 and 191. The Delhi High Court stayed challans in 2018 and the Madras High Court is reported to have upheld the ban, so enforcement varies by state.

Wheels much larger than stock, loud exhausts, coloured or flashing exterior lights and underbody neons draw fines, and undeclared modifications can lead to rejected insurance claims. The guides saying this are not official sources.
High Security Registration Plates are mandatory, so a plate designer can only sell frames and display plates. From general knowledge, not re-checked.
